abstracts.abstract: Engineering informatics has long struggled with heterogeneous knowledge representation across complex system lifecycles. This paper introduces a novel ontological paradigm called Context-Aware Knowledge Evolution Framework (CAKEF) that fundamentally reconceptualizes how engineering knowledge is captured, represented, and utilized throughout the product lifecycle. Unlike traditional ontology engineering approaches that treat knowledge as static structures, CAKEF introduces dynamic knowledge graphs that evolve through contextual interactions and semantic reasoning. The framework employs a multi-layered ontology architecture integrating semantic web technologies with temporal reasoning capabilities, enabling machines to understand not only what engineering knowledge exists but why it changes and how it should adapt across different engineering design phases. We validate the framework through comprehensive case studies in mechanical design and building information modeling contexts, demonstrating that CAKEF achieves 47% improvement in knowledge retrieval accuracy and 62% reduction in semantic ambiguity compared to state-of-the-art ontology engineering methods. The proposed paradigm shift from static to dynamic knowledge representation addresses fundamental limitations in current engineering informatics approaches and opens new research directions for adaptive decision support systems that learn and evolve with engineering projects. This work contributes to both the theoretical foundations of knowledge engineering and practical applications in complex engineering systems.

Semantic web technologies have shown promise in engineering design informatics, yet existing ontology alignment methods suffer from limited scalability and poor handling of domain-specific semantic gaps. This paper presents an enhanced ontology matching framework that significantly improves semantic interoperability in engineering knowledge bases. The proposed approach integrates transformer-based embeddings with a novel semantic similarity metric that accounts for engineering-specific terminology hierarchies and contextual usage patterns. We introduce a hierarchical matching algorithm that progressively resolves entity correspondences across multiple abstraction levels, from lexical to conceptual to structural alignment. Evaluation conducted on benchmark ontology alignment datasets demonstrates that our framework achieves 12% higher F1-score than current state-of-the-art methods while reducing computational complexity by 35%. Furthermore, we validate the framework's effectiveness in integrating heterogeneous building information modeling ontologies with machine learning models for engineering data analytics. The improved ontology engineering methodology provides a more robust foundation for knowledge management in complex engineering domains, enabling better decision support and information reuse across organizational boundaries.

This paper presents an innovative cyber-physical system architecture for real-time engineering data integration that fundamentally transforms how information flows across the product lifecycle. The proposed system, named Intelligent Engineering Data Fabric (IEDF), leverages Internet of Things sensors, edge computing, and semantic web technologies to create a unified knowledge representation layer that spans from conceptual design to manufacturing and operations. Unlike conventional engineering data integration approaches that rely on point-to-point integrations, IEDF employs a novel knowledge graph-based middleware that automatically discovers, categorizes, and semantically links engineering data regardless of format or source. The system architecture incorporates machine learning models for anomaly detection and predictive quality assurance, enabling proactive decision support in engineering processes. Implementation and validation through a collaborative robotics manufacturing scenario demonstrate that IEDF reduces data integration development time by 68% and improves engineering change response time by 54%. The architectural paradigm established by IEDF represents a new direction for digital transformation in engineering, providing the infrastructure foundation for smart factories and intelligent design environments that require seamless information exchange across heterogeneous systems.

Design decision support in building information modeling environments remains challenging due to fragmented information and，缺乏统一的知识表示机制。 This paper presents an improved decision support system that integrates enhanced data mining techniques with building information modeling workflows. The proposed system employs a hybrid machine learning architecture combining supervised learning for performance prediction with reinforcement learning for design optimization, all wrapped within an intuitive visual analytics interface. Key improvements over existing systems include: (1) a novel feature engineering pipeline that automatically extracts design-relevant attributes from BIM models, (2) an improved recommendation engine that provides context-aware suggestions considering design history and project-specific constraints, and (3) a scalable knowledge management module that learns from past design decisions. Validation through four real-world architecture projects demonstrates that the improved system reduces design iteration time by 41% and improves energy performance of designs by 23% compared to conventional BIM-based decision approaches. The work provides engineering practitioners with a powerful tool for evidence-based design and establishes a reference architecture for integrating advanced data analytics capabilities into mainstream building information modeling practice.
